summary: Today’s pulse tracks Footage of Tibet floods isn't being shown in China - and we know little about victims there, Police arrest seven more men in aftermath of deadly A66 crash, and Nepal-Tibet flash flood: number of missing people in Nepal rises to 1,924 – latest updates. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are people, rescue, and crash. In the background, Large fire near Wembley Stadium disrupts tube and rail services and Trump arch will alter sightlines of many Washington DC landmarks, report says keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Footage of Tibet floods isn't being shown in China - and we know little about victims there
headlines.description: Some of the most dramatic footage from the deadly flash flooding is hidden from public view in China.

headlines.title: Police arrest seven more men in aftermath of deadly A66 crash
headlines.description: Cleveland police say a total of 24 people arrested in investigation after crash that killed two officers Seven more men have been arrested as part of an operation tackling alleged organised crime after the head-on crash on the A66 that resulted in seven deaths, Cleveland police have said. Officers said four men, aged 21, 25, 35 and 40, were being held on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life after a vehicle crashed into a house in Steele Crescent, Middlesbrough.

headlines.title: Nepal-Tibet flash flood: number of missing people in Nepal rises to 1,924 – latest updates
headlines.description: Nepali disaster authority confirms jump of more than 400 in total of those unaccounted for, with 584 deaths confirmed in Nepal and five in Tibet Flood rescue efforts resume Visual guide: how the deadly flooding unfolded More now on the Nepali army’s rescue operation to save about 100 people trapped in a tunnel at a hydropower project swamped by Wednesday’s flooding . “Two helicopters have been dispatched but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel,” army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet told AFP. Relief efforts are also under way to provide the rescued people what they need. The army is still working to safely evacuate more than 100 people trapped in the same tunnel.

headlines.title: Large fire near Wembley Stadium disrupts tube and rail services
headlines.description: About 125 firefighters tackle blaze at Neasden waste facility as nearby Amazon warehouse is evacuated A large fire has broken out at a waste facility close to Wembley Stadium in north-west London, disrupting tube and train lines in the area. Twenty fire engines and about 125 firefighters were sent to tackle the blaze at a mixed-waste facility on an industrial estate in Neasden, less than a mile from the venue.

headlines.title: Trump arch will alter sightlines of many Washington DC landmarks, report says
headlines.description: National Park Service, which backs the 250ft arch, says it is likely to disrupt historical significance of dozens of sites A new National Park Service report backs Donald Trump ’s proposed arch, despite what it says are adverse effects to the sightlines of a host of landmarks in Washington, including the Washington Monument and the Lincoln and Jefferson memorials. The report released on Friday says the 250ft-tall (76-meter) memorial arch is likely to disrupt the historical significance of dozens of sites near its planned location adjacent to the Arlington Memorial Bridge.

headlines.title: Volunteers rescue man stuck on 10,000ft-high ledge in Sierra Nevada
headlines.description: Climber, stuck on 6in ridge, had veered off treacherous path and ‘any fall would almost certainly be fatal’ An ill-fated move left a man stranded on a 6in ledge over 10,000ft off the ground for hours in California’s Sierra Nevada mountain range, before a volunteer rescue team came to his aid. The climber, who has not been publicly identified, had been scaling the Mendenhall couloir, a gully on the face of Laurel mountain, with a friend on Saturday.

headlinePool.title: Milo Yiannopoulos, a far-right political commentator, detained by ICE
headlinePool.description: A former editor of Breitbart News, Yiannopoulos has also served as an intern for Marjorie Taylor Greene Milo Yiannopoulos, a far-right British political commentator, was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Louisiana, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). In a statement on Friday, a DHS spokesperson said that Yiannopoulos was arrested on Thursday at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans international airport (MSY). The spokesperson said Yiannopoulos “legally entered the country” in May 2019, but that “he chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws”.
